title: Design exercise: SAA-2.2-S08
scenario: Marlowe Freight Tracking depends on three tools written by an engineer who has left: a cron job that snapshots volumes, database instances and tables nightly and prunes them by name, a heartbeat script that repoints DNS records at the second Region when the first stops answering, and a Python replicator that copies tracking events between tables in two Regions with home-made conflict handling. Each has failed silently at least once this year. The team of five has no capacity to rewrite them, and management wants no custom resilience code at all. Both Regions accept tracking writes, and last-writer-wins is acceptable.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
Management requires zero custom code for backup, failover or replication
Both Regions must keep accepting tracking writes
Backups must be kept for 30 days

rubric.label: Each of the three homegrown tools is replaced by a managed service and none is rebuilt on servers
Both Regions stay writable, with conflicts resolved last-writer-wins, and 30-day backup retention is met

constraint_reason: Mapped as design_exercise to complete skill coverage when no dedicated live lab step exists
